title: Klunk paper profile
description: The rules for one kind of paper: how many sections, what each is worth, which question types belong in it. Everything a previous generation of this toolchain hardcoded lives here as data, so a new course is a file rather than a code change.

syllabusId.description: The syllabus model this profile assesses. Klunk uses it to offer the right topics when building a paper, and to report coverage.

courseId.description: Which course within that model, e.g. the Year 9 of a 7-10 syllabus, or SL of an IB one. A subject runs across several years and each year sets its own papers, so without this every year of a subject is one undifferentiated pool of questions. Absent means the profile assesses the whole model, which is what every profile written before this field meant and still means. Only meaningful alongside syllabusId: a bare course id could belong to any model in the folder.

instructions.description: General instructions for the cover page, one per line.

cover.description: How this paper's cover sheet differs from the folder's school.json. The two real covers that shaped this share a skeleton and differ in exactly these two ways, so everything else stays in one place.

identification.description: Overrides the folder's identification fields for this kind of paper. An external-style trial prints a student number grid where an internal exam prints Name and Class.

marksAwardedColumn.description: Print the marks breakdown as a Section / Marks Available / Marks Awarded table with a '/ N' cell per row for the marker, rather than as a list. Internal school exams do this and public examinations do not.

questionTypes.description: Types this course uses at all. Klunk hides every other type from the editor, which is how a Design and Technology teacher never sees an SQL question type.

wholeNumberTotals.description: Whether each question's total must be a whole number. Part marks within a question are still allowed.

print.description: How the paper is laid out when printed. Klunk renders HTML and prints to PDF via the browser, so these map onto CSS.

answerLineSpacingMm.description: Spacing of ruled answer lines. Marks per line is the usual way schools size answer space.

linesPerMark.description: How much ruled space a mark earns, when the question does not say.

identificationField.description: Duplicated verbatim from school.schema.json, which is where it is documented. Repeated rather than referenced because a cross-file $ref would need a registry the validation script does not build.

section.description: Constraints are drawn from 11 years of real papers (2015-2025), so they distinguish what is genuinely fixed from what varies year to year.

questionCount.description: Exact number of questions, where the section always has the same count. HSC Design and Technology Section I is always 10; Section III is always 1.

minQuestions.description: Use instead of questionCount where the count varies. Section II ran 2, 3 and 4 questions across 2015-2025, so pinning it to one number would reject valid papers.

marksPerQuestion.description: Set where every question in the section is worth the same, e.g. 1 mark per objective-response question.
